examples.question_text: Car $A$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}34\\12\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and car $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}18\\24\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$ and its relative speed.

The velocity of vehicle $A$ relative to vehicle $B$ is $\begin{pmatrix}-8\\11\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Vehicle $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}32\\-4\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the velocity and speed of $A$.

Ship $A$ has velocity $4\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and ship $B$ has velocity $9\underset{\sim}{i}+15\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north. Find the bearing on which $A$ appears to move from $B$, to the nearest degree.
A ferry travels due north at $12$ km/h relative to the water. A current flows due east at $5$ km/h. Find the ferry's velocity relative to the bank, its speed and its bearing to the nearest degree.
A plane must have ground velocity $\begin{pmatrix}0\\280\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. The wind has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}30\\-40\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the plane's required velocity relative to the air.

A boat has speed $13$ km/h in still water. A current flows due east at $5$ km/h. The boat must travel due north relative to the bank. Find its steering bearing to the nearest degree and its speed relative to the bank.

At noon, drone $A$ is at $(2,3)$ km and drone $B$ is at $(14,7)$ km. Their constant velocities are $\begin{pmatrix}20\\8\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and $\begin{pmatrix}12\\14\end{pmatrix}$ km/h respectively. Find the position of $B$ relative to $A$ after $30$ minutes and their separation then.
examples.solution_text:
Let $t$ be hours after noon. Then $30$ minutes is $0.5$ hours.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_A(0.5)&=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}+0.5\begin{pmatrix}20\\8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}12\\7\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_B(0.5)&=\begin{pmatrix}14\\7\end{pmatrix}+0.5\begin{pmatrix}12\\14\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}20\\14\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_{BA}(0.5)&=\underset{\sim}{r}_B(0.5)-\underset{\sim}{r}_A(0.5)\\&=\begin{pmatrix}20\\14\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}12\\7\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}8\\7\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Separation}&=\sqrt{8^2+7^2}\\&=\sqrt{113}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A launch is $42$ km due east of a patrol boat. Both travel due east at constant speeds: the launch at $12$ km/h and the patrol boat at $26$ km/h. How long does the patrol boat take to catch the launch?
examples.solution_text:
Take $\underset{\sim}{i}$ due east.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}_{PL}&=26\underset{\sim}{i}-12\underset{\sim}{i}\\&=14\underset{\sim}{i}\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$

Relative to the launch, the patrol boat closes the $42$ km gap at $14$ km/h.

$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{42}{14}\\&=3\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Subtracting gives (34−18,12−24)=(16,−12) km/h. Its magnitude is √(256+144)=20 km/h.
Rearranging gives v_A=v_AB+v_B=(−8+32,11−4)=(24,7) km/h. Speed is √(576+49)=25 km/h.

Relative velocity is (4−9,3−15)=(−5,−12) km/h, pointing south-west. The angle west of south is arctan(5/12)=22.6199°. Bearing is 202.6199°, rounded to 203°. The diagram's endpoint, components and angle arc agree.

Adding water and current velocities gives (5,12) km/h. Speed is √(25+144)=13 km/h. Bearing is arctan(5/12)=22.6199°, rounded to 023°. The head-to-tail diagram correctly represents both givens and the resultant.
Required air velocity is (0,280)−(30,−40)=(−30,320) km/h. Diagram vectors O→A=(−0.6,6.4), A→G=(0.6,−0.8) and O→G=(0,5.6) use one consistent scale and satisfy air plus wind equals ground.

Cancelling the eastward current requires a=−5. Fixed speed gives 25+b²=169; northward travel selects b=12. Steering bearing is 360°−arctan(5/12)=337.3801°, rounded to 337°. Bank velocity is (0,12) km/h, with speed 12 km/h. Diagram vectors and angle agree.
After 0.5 hours, A is (2,3)+0.5(20,8)=(12,7) km and B is (14,7)+0.5(12,14)=(20,14) km. B relative to A is (8,7) km; separation is √(64+49)=√113 km.
The patrol boat's velocity relative to the launch is (26−12)i=14i km/h. It closes the 42 km eastward gap in 42/14=3 hours.
